sections.heading: Why we are writing to you

sentences.text: We are writing because public records show that CHD2-related epileptic encephalopathy and SCN1A-related seizure disorders are both linked to a picture of too little working protein from one copy being lost, with loss of function recorded for each condition.

Public records also show a high phenotype similarity between the two conditions, with overlap in seizure features such as atonic seizures, generalized myoclonic seizures, tonic seizures, febrile seizures in early childhood, and seizures brought on by febrile infection.
We hope to learn from a community that is further along in research, studies, and trial planning.
Gene2Phenotype lists both the CHD2 and SCN1A disease links as definitive.
Public records show patient organizations in both spaces, with Coalition to Cure CHD2 for our community and Dravet Syndrome Foundation listed for yours.

Public records show registry or natural history activity in both areas, including the CHD2 Natural History Project, the Coalition to Cure CHD2 registry, Simons Searchlight, RARE-X Data Collection Program, and Citizen Health for CHD2, and studies NCT06504511 and NCT06967727 plus Simons Searchlight for SCN1A.
Published records also show disease models in both fields, with 17 PubMed records for CHD2 and 257 for SCN1A.
NIH Reporter shows active NIH-funded research in both areas in FY2025-2026, with 4 projects for CHD2 and 8 for SCN1A.

sections.heading: What we would like to learn from or reuse

sentences.text: Public records suggest that registry design and natural history protocols may carry over well enough to review together, because the clinical picture overlaps, though age of onset and severity still need checking before anything is adopted.
The same is true for outcome measures and endpoints.

Public records also suggest that your clinical network, sites, and investigators may be a useful starting point for us to understand, including links through Simons Searchlight, Dravet Syndrome Foundation, and SCN1A studies such as NCT07531745, NCT06872125, NCT05419492, and NCT06283212.
We would also value learning how your community has approached trial design, since public records show several targeted SCN1A studies that may offer a template for discussion with experts.

We found no public record of a targeted clinical trial for CHD2 in the sources searched, while ClinicalTrials.gov records show gene-level SCN1A trials, including antisense and gene therapy programs, with the highest phase listed as phase 3.

We also found no public record of an approved disease-specific therapy for CHD2, while FDA-labeled therapies named for Dravet syndrome are listed for your community, including cannabidiol, fenfluramine, and stiripentol.

At the same time, the two communities must not assume that a therapeutic strategy transfers directly, because published SCN1A cases include more than one mechanism direction, the recorded mechanism is gene-and-disease level rather than family level, and a clinical geneticist needs to confirm the mechanism class of a family's own variant.
We also must not assume that SCN1A disease models can stand in for CHD2 disease models, because the model is specific to its gene, even if some assay ideas may still be worth expert review.

We cannot assume enrolment in SCN1A studies for CHD2 families, because a ClinicalTrials.gov record states that eligibility can depend on variant class, and one SCN1A study excludes gain-of-function variants.
Do the age of onset and typical severity of SCN1A-related disease match ours closely enough for its registry items and outcome measures to apply.
Is the patient organization listed for SCN1A the right contact, and does it run a registry.
SCN1A variants are reported with more than one mechanism, so which class does a family's own variant belong to, and has that been shown functionally.
Has a child's specific CHD2 variant been functionally classified as loss of function, gain of function, or dominant negative, and does it match the mechanism recorded for the condition.
What functional evidence exists for CHD2, since the recorded mechanism is inferred from variant types rather than direct functional studies.
Thank you for reading.

glossary.meaning: A change that leaves a gene copy working less well or not working.
The features seen in a condition, such as seizure types, age of onset, and development.
A study that follows people over time to learn how a condition changes.
An outcome a study measures, such as seizure count or daily function.
A change in a gene's DNA sequence.
A doctor with specialist training in how gene changes relate to health and disease.
